newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico eyes 100,000 new rubber hectares - Ag Min.
newsitem.headline: Mexico eyes 100,000 new rubber hectares - Ag Min.

text.p: Mexican Agriculture Minister Francisco Labastida Ochoa said the country is eyeing the possibility of planting 100,000 new hectares with rubber trees in the next four years.

In a statement obtained Tuesday, the ministry said Lastida told a farmers meeting that the country needed to boost rubber production in prime south-eastern states to offset its heavy reliance on rubber imports.
Labastida said Mexico imports annually around 90 percent of its rubber needs, which amount to between 75,000 and 80,000 tonnes per year.
Mexico's 1995-1996 production ended at around 10,800 tonnes, only a tad higher than the previous cycle, according to figures from the Mexican Rubber Council.

Rubber experts reckon Mexico needs to plant around 40,000 more hectares to become self-sufficient in the future, although even more surface area could be planted to export natural rubber to the North American market.
The United States and Canada consume about 1.2 million tonnes annually.
